# Separate foreground recovery and best-effort saves from background execution

## Platform difference

Lifecycle callbacks can initiate recovery or persistence, but they do not guarantee asynchronous work completes before suspension or termination.

## Implementation

InkNote flushes pending saves on inactive/paused/detached; its unawaited calls are best-effort. Its Rust storage uses temporary files, sync and rename and reconstructs metadata after corrupt JSON. SSH Codex preserves an existing transport when a foreground model probe is slow/rejected, disconnecting only for its explicit transport error. Minecraft Box has shared pause/resume/dispose and reconnect cancellation, not a native OH background service.

## Applicability

These are shared application mechanisms exercised by OH lifecycle transitions. Keep transport connectivity, application-server responsiveness and durable save completion as separate observable states.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A failed feature probe need not mean the SSH transport is dead. A callback starting a save is not proof that data reached disk. Native atomic-write source code alone does not establish crash durability on the target filesystem.

## Verification

Test rapid background/foreground transitions, delayed servers, actual disconnection, process termination during save, restart recovery and cancellation of stale reconnect attempts.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
